### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Question

This is a newbie question but i can't wrap my head around a working solution.  

Basically I use mini.files as my default file explorer but i'd like on nvim launch that mini.files doesn't open if a (mk)session has been auto loaded (I use persistence.nvim).  
I do have an event to detect when a session has been successfully loaded on startup but i can't prevent mini.files from appearing. It seems mini.files opens way after this event and calling close at this moment does nothing (yet).   

Any idea how to solve this ?  
Thank you for your help.   

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
  pattern = 'PersistenceLoadPost',
  callback = function()
    require('mini.files').close()
  end,
})
```

comment_data.body:
> Basically I use mini.files as my default file explorer but i'd like on nvim launch that mini.files doesn't open if a (mk)session has been auto loaded (I use persistence.nvim).
> I do have an event to detect when a session has been successfully loaded on startup but i can't prevent mini.files from appearing. It seems mini.files opens way after this event and calling close at this moment does nothing (yet).

'mini.files' doesn't open on startup with if Neovim is started as `nvim` from command line. The "default explorer" functionality means that 'mini.files' will open if Neovim is started like `nvim .` / `nvim path/to/directory` *or* inside running Neovim instance executing `:edit .` / `:edit path/to/directory`.

So the answer to "How to conditionally prevent mini.files from opening on startup?" is to not start Neovim in a way that tries to edit a directory. My guess is that either there is some shell alias that opens Neovim like `nvim .` or a session contains a buffer that is for directory.

The answer to "How to hide 'mini.files' after session is loaded?" is probably to use `vim.schedule`. So the `callback`'s body is something like `vim.schedule(require('mini.files').close)`. This *might* work because opening explorer for directory editing is itself delayed (for technical reasons). Note that this might result in a flicker as explorer might be briefly opened and closed.

A more robust yet more complex solution is to create (inside callback for `PersistenceLoadPost`) a temporary autocommand for [`MiniFilesExplorerOpen`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/581724ebb39f4aa70bdbffb891d57d6141d29035/doc/mini-files.txt#L330) event that immediately closes 'mini.files'. Be sure to delete this autocommand very soon to be able to open 'mini.files' explorer at all.

reply_data.body:
Yes, i forgot to mention but i do tend to use `nvim .`   to open nvim.
Is this an unusual way to do it ? I quite don't get the distinction between `nvim` and `nvim .`

I found out in `nvim_create_autocmd` documentation a magic parameter `once` that removes the autocmd after the first execution, works like a charm.

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
  pattern = 'MiniFilesExplorerOpen',
  once = true,
  callback = function()
    require('mini.files').close()
  end,
})
```

Thank you for your help !

> I found out in `nvim_create_autocmd` documentation a magic parameter `once` that removes the autocmd after the first execution, works like a charm.

Yes, there is one. But beware that with this solution the first time opening explorer will fail whenever you *won't* start Neovim as `nvim .`.
